stories.head: The hidden costs distorting your AI ROI
stories.plain: Integration, oversight, data preparation, and displaced work can make AI productivity gains look much smaller on the balance sheet than they appear in demos. This matters for every marketing team justifying AI spend — true AI ROI requires accounting for the full cost stack, not just model licensing fees.

stories.head: The Data Tax You're Now Paying Per Token — with Ben Schein from Domo
stories.plain: Domo's Chief AI and Analytics Officer argues that bad data quality now appears directly on your AI invoice — every messy input costs real money each time a model runs. It reframes data hygiene from a back-office concern into a direct line-item budget issue for marketers buying or building AI.

stories.head: Bazaarvoice Launches AI Visibility Package to Optimize Brand Content for AI Recommendations
stories.plain: Bazaarvoice is packaging UGC and brand content specifically to appear in AI-driven product recommendations, claiming early clients see a 40% lift in AI-referred traffic. This is a concrete commercial product built around GEO — making it one of the first scaled tools helping brands get onto the AI shelf rather than the search results page.

stories.head: Descope Unveils Cross-App Access to Let Enterprises Manage AI Agent Identity with Existing Providers
stories.plain: Descope now lets companies plug AI agent identity and permissions into whatever identity provider they already use, via ID-JAG token support. As agentic systems gain access to customer data and campaign tools, controlling what agents are allowed to do — and proving it — becomes a core governance requirement.

stories.head: Scrunch's Kevin White: Being Cited by AI, Not Just Found, Is the New Marketing Frontier
stories.plain: The head of marketing at Scrunch (now Sitecore) explains why ChatGPT referral traffic metrics miss most of AI's impact — the real game is getting cited inside AI answers where no click ever happens. He outlines what agent-ready pages and long-tail intent structuring look like in practice, making this a practical GEO primer.

stories.head: Optimizely Introduces Purpose-Built AI Models for Marketing at Lower Cost
stories.plain: Optimizely is shipping a family of post-trained, marketing-specific AI models instead of routing tasks through generic frontier LLMs. The claim is frontier-level quality at a fraction of the cost. This matters because it signals a shift in how marketing AI is bought — task-specific fine-tuned models may undercut the big-model bundling strategy that vendors like Adobe and Salesforce rely on.

stories.head: Anthropic-Salesforce Deal Makes Salesforce's Interface Optional via Claude
stories.plain: A Claudeforce integration puts Salesforce data and workflows directly inside Claude, meaning users may never open Salesforce again. This is a structural shift in how enterprise marketing software is accessed — AI becomes the interface, not the app. It reshapes buying decisions and raises real questions about which platform actually owns the customer relationship going forward.

stories.head: Optimizely Virtual Teammates Give Marketers Role-Specific AI Coworkers
stories.plain: Optimizely's Virtual Teammates are persistent AI agents that retain context across sessions, take on recurring marketing tasks proactively, and operate inside defined identity and permissions. This is a concrete example of agentic AI entering the marketing workflow with governance guardrails baked in — directly relevant to anyone evaluating how AI changes staffing and platform investment.

stories.head: The Hidden Costs Distorting Your AI ROI
stories.plain: Integration work, data preparation, human oversight, and displaced labor quietly eat the gains that AI productivity numbers advertise. The piece gives a practical framework for auditing true AI cost versus reported ROI. For anyone building a business case or approving AI spend, this is essential reading before signing a contract or scaling a deployment.

stories.head: Scrunch's Kevin White: Being Cited in AI Answers Matters More Than Referral Traffic
stories.plain: Kevin White (now at Sitecore via Scrunch) argues that ChatGPT referral clicks undercount AI-driven influence — most AI citations never generate a trackable visit. He outlines what agent-ready pages and long-tail intent structuring actually look like in practice. For marketers still thinking about GEO as an SEO add-on, this reframes it as a fundamental content architecture problem.

month.skicker: 30-day synthesis · the shape underneath the feed

themes.head: AI agents need identity & governance rails before they scale
body: As AI agents proliferate across marketing stacks, they are acquiring permissions, accessing data, and acting autonomously — yet most enterprises have no framework for controlling what those agents can do or as whom they act. Descope's Cross-App Access launch and the Anthropic–Salesforce partnership both signal that identity management for non-human actors is becoming a first-class infrastructure problem.

Martech's own coverage flags a governance test most marketers are failing: knowing which agent touched which decision and why. Without audit trails and scoped permissions, autonomous stacks carry hidden liability that legal and security teams have not yet priced in — making governance the unsexy blocker on every AI roadmap.

themes.head: AI-native visibility: being cited, not just ranked
body: Search engine optimization is giving way to a new discipline: making your brand legible to AI recommendation engines. Bazaarvoice's AI Visibility package and Scrunch's analysis of ChatGPT referral traffic both point to the same shift — the retrieval logic of LLMs is now a distribution channel, and brands must structure content so AI systems will cite them, not merely index them.

The stakes are higher than a ranking change. When an AI agent acts on behalf of a consumer — comparing products, booking services — a brand that is not in the model's trusted corpus simply does not exist at the moment of decision. Marketers need content & UGC strategies built around machine readability, structured authority signals, and explicit factual claims.

Agile Brand · cited not just found

themes.head: The hidden cost of AI: data tax, ROI distortion, bad inputs
body: Three separate threads converged this month on a single warning: the cost of running AI in marketing is systematically underestimated. The per-token 'data tax' (Domo's Ben Schein), distorted ROI calculations that ignore inference and integration overhead, and the compounding error rate when AI operates on dirty CRM data — all point to a financial reckoning that CFOs will force in 2027 budget cycles.

Marketers already know their data is bad; AI is simply making that fact undeniable at speed and scale. Purpose-built, cheaper models from Optimizely and Phonely's Alma (84% cheaper than OpenAI for voice) show one escape route — right-sizing models to tasks — but the deeper fix is data hygiene investment that most teams have deferred for years.
ev: MarTech · hidden costs distorting AI ROI
Agile Brand · data tax per token

themes.head: Role-specific AI coworkers replace generic copilots
body: The generic 'ask AI anything' interface is being replaced by purpose-built agents with defined roles, permissions, and domain knowledge. Optimizely's Virtual Teammates give marketers role-specific AI coworkers; Archive's Archie agent vets influencer creators rather than just surfacing them; Yodeck's agent manages digital signage end-to-end. Specificity is becoming the differentiator — vendors are competing on how narrowly and expertly their agent understands one job.

This shift has real procurement implications. Buyers should stop evaluating AI features and start evaluating AI roles: what decisions does this agent own, what data does it need, and what human signs off. The Optimizely purpose-built model announcement reinforces that frontier-model quality is no longer the moat — workflow fit and cost efficiency are.
ev: Agile Brand · Archive Archie creator-vetting agent
MarTech Series · Yodeck AI agent signage

themes.head: Cross-platform connected AI workflows dissolve channel silos
body: Advertisers are demanding that AI orchestration span channels without requiring manual re-entry or separate dashboards. Innovid's NIVO expanding into Meta Ads via MCP integration, the Anthropic–Salesforce deal making the CRM interface optional, and Trifecta's Claude partnership for enterprise workflows all illustrate a platform layer emerging above individual channel tools — where AI reads signals from one channel and acts in another.

For marketers, the decision this forces is architectural: do you let each vendor build its own agentic layer, or do you invest in a neutral orchestration plane that preserves data fidelity across channels? The measurement corollary, covered in MarTech's ad-attribution piece, is that incrementality testing now has to account for AI actions that blur the line between touchpoint and conversion.

month.takeaway: Every major move this month — cheaper models, role-specific agents, AI-native SEO, governance tooling, cross-channel orchestration — is a response to the same underlying pressure: AI is now making consequential marketing decisions faster than human oversight, cost controls, or data quality can keep up.
